records.name: Team Philly Race Training
records.summary: A paid season program, offered through the Philadelphia Runner store, that trains runners for spring and fall races. A season membership includes weekly group runs and training plans, and race entries cost extra.
records.what_you_do: Train with a group for a spring or fall race. The membership brings weekly group runs, supported Saturday long runs, clinics, info sessions and team social events.

schedule.text: Weekly group runs come with a season membership. The program page does not list run days, times or a meeting spot.

cost.text: Season memberships: $125 spring, $150 fall half marathon, $175 fall marathon, $250 full year. Race entries are not included.

first_step.how: Buy a season membership on the RunSignUp program page, which lists four options.
first_step.basis: The program is for beginner to intermediate runners, but a paid membership comes before you can see the group runs, and the page does not say how a new runner starts.
first_step.what_to_expect: The page does not describe a typical group run, so ask the program about run times and distances before you pay. Members get a training plan for the race they pick, weekly group runs, supported Saturday long runs, and team clinics and social events. Race registration is separate and is not included in the membership.
first_visit_tips: Pick the membership that matches your race: spring, fall half marathon, fall marathon, or the full year.
Register for each race separately, since the membership does not include race entries.
Ask about run times and the meeting spot before you pay, since the page does not list them.

records.notes: The program page shows the 2026 season (Feb 20 to Nov 29, 2026). Membership start dates (2/21 and 8/1) have no year on the page. Run days, times, the meeting spot, distances and coaches are not published on the program page or the store page, so the first visit cannot be described in detail. The refund policy is a separate page that was not read. The address is the program's listed place and is not confirmed as the group run meeting point. The October 31 free All City long run is a one-time promotion with no year, so it is left out. Fetches used: 4.

records.name: Team Up Philly
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs free sports and enrichment programs for girls in Philadelphia, including tutoring, an after-school Girls Club and a leadership academy for high school girls.
records.what_you_do: Girls join a free after-school Girls Club for grades 4 to 8, a free summer camp for grades 4 to 12, or the G.I.R.L.S. Leadership Academy for grades 9 to 12. Volunteers can coach, tutor or speak to the girls, and the group also runs summer scholarships and events.

schedule.text: Girls Club meets Mondays and Wednesdays from 3:30 to 5:15 pm, fall through spring. Other programs run on their own schedules, which the site does not list.

locations.label: Girls Club at John Barry Elementary

cost.text: Programs are free, per the program pages.

first_step.how: Register your girl through the TeamSnap form linked from the Team Up Philly programs page; the programs are free.
first_step.basis: Programs are free and open to girls in the listed grades through a clear registration button, though the site does not describe a first day or a welcome for newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Girls Club meets twice a week after school at Bluford or John Barry Elementary, or at the Daroff Rec Center during the Rebuild construction, and Team Up Philly provides rides to Daroff at dismissal. Sessions mix fitness drills, basketball basics, tennis and yoga with talks on teamwork, goal-setting and self-care, and the girls complete a community service project. The program is free, and the site does not list start or end dates for the season.
first_visit_tips: Register through the TeamSnap form on the programs page; the site lists no deadline, so register early.
Be ready at dismissal on Monday or Wednesday, since pick-up is by 5:30 pm.
If your school is under construction, ask which site your girl goes to, since some girls attend Daroff.
Ask about gear and any forms before the first day, since the page does not list them.

records.notes: The office is in Narberth, outside Philadelphia. The programs meet in Philadelphia: Girls Club at Bluford and John Barry Elementary, and the Daroff Rec Center during construction. The site does not give meeting places for the Leadership Academy or the summer camps. The site describes its girls as living in under-served Philadelphia communities but gives no neighborhood or income rule, so the audience stays public. The volunteer page says up-to-date clearances are required without naming them, so background_check is recorded as true and Act 153 is left out. Volunteer sign-up is by email only. The home page names a tutoring and academic support section, but the programs page lists no tutoring program; testimonials mention tutors meeting girls at Friends' Central on Thursdays. Flag Football is on the program list with no page of its own. Fetches used: 5.

records.name: Temple Beth Zion-Beth Israel (BZBI)
records.summary: A Jewish congregation at 300 South 18th Street in Center City. It holds Shabbat morning services in person and on Zoom, weekday morning minyanim, family and early childhood education, and adult learning classes.
records.what_you_do: Join Shabbat morning services or a weekday minyan, take an adult class such as the introduction to Judaism or the book club, or ask the office about the Shabbat dinners for young professionals. Membership and dues are handled through the office.

schedule.text: Shabbat morning service at 9:30 am on Saturdays, in the Goldberg Sanctuary and on Zoom for most in-person services. Weekday morning minyanim run every morning, with the times on the worship schedule, and a prayer gathering is held on the first Friday night of each month.

cost.text: The site lists no dollar amounts for membership dues. It says dues are set around each family's situation so that membership stays affordable.

first_step.how: Call the Temple Office at 215-735-5148 with your questions before you come to Saturday morning services at 9:30 am.
first_step.basis: The worship page says anyone interested in minyan is welcome, the Visiting Us page tells you to call the office, and the adult learning page says no one is turned away from congregational learning. The site does not describe a first-visit routine, so it is not rated 5.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shabbat morning services start at 9:30 am in the Goldberg Sanctuary, and most in-person services can also be joined on Zoom once you get the password from the office. Weekday minyanim are morning prayer gatherings open to anyone interested, and a Torah study with Rabbi Mort follows the Wednesday minyan at about 8:15 am. The site does not say how long services last, what visitors wear, or whether you must register first.
first_visit_tips: Call the Temple Office at 215-735-5148 or email templeoffice@bzbi.org; weekday hours are 9 am to 5 pm, and Friday hours end at 3 pm.
For pick-up or drop-off by car, call the office to reserve a parking pass; metered street parking is also nearby.
Ask the office for the Zoom password if you would rather join online.
The office is closed on federal holidays and many Jewish holidays, so call ahead on those days.

records.notes: The Visiting Us page is at /worship/visiting_us/; the /visiting-us path returned 404. The weekday minyan times sit in a chart that the text view could not read, so the schedule points to the worship page. Tier 1 listed a Sunday minyan and schmooze; the worship page read this run did not mention Sunday, so Sunday stays in the days list until someone confirms it. Adult learning has some fee-based classes and events, with scholarships available, and no amounts are given. The adult learning page lists an introduction to Judaism course, but gives no dates for it. No SEPTA stop is named on the site and none is on the same block, so none is listed. Fetches used: 6 (one 404).

records.name: Temple Contemporary
records.summary: A free contemporary art gallery on the first floor of Temple's Tyler School of Art and Architecture. It has exhibitions, lectures and public events, and anyone can attend.
records.what_you_do: Walk through the free exhibitions during open hours, or come to an evening public event such as a game night or an artist party. The gallery lists no public volunteer, docent, class or workshop program.

schedule.text: Open Tuesday to Saturday, 11 am to 6 pm, with free admission. Evening events are scheduled from time to time and listed on the gallery's event pages.

locations.label: Temple Contemporary gallery, Norris Street entrance

first_step.how: Come in during open hours, or check the gallery's event pages and come to a public evening event.
first_step.basis: Admission is free and the gallery is open to the public during posted hours, and evening events are open to anyone. The site does not mention beginners or a special welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Open hours are a self-guided visit: you walk through the exhibitions at your own pace at no charge. Evening events are more social, such as a game night with board games, puzzles and snacks, or an artist party. The events page lists each event's date and time, so check it before an evening visit.
first_visit_tips: Enter on Norris Street, between 12th and 13th streets, inside Tyler School of Art and Architecture.
Check the events page for the date and time before an evening visit, since evening events are not on a fixed schedule.
For access questions, call 215-777-9090, the number the site lists for 'not sure where to start' questions; the page does not describe gallery access, so ask about step-free entry.
Parking and transit are not described on the gallery page, so plan your trip before you go.

records.notes: This is a university gallery and event venue. It has no public volunteer, docent or class program on the gallery, events or public programming pages, so it is published as a free place to visit. The owner may want to decide whether venues like this belong in the directory; the verdict for a building would be not_a_group. Physical access (entrance, steps, restrooms, elevator) and sensory or quiet hours are not described on any page read; the accessibility page covers Temple services in general. The exhibitions running Aug 25 to Dec 5, 2026 and the Oct 15 and Oct 30 events are one-time listings, so they are kept out of schedule.text. The Oct 21 artist talk and the Nov 13 MFA open studios are Tyler-wide events rather than gallery programs, so they are left out. Fetches used: 4.

records.name: Temple University Music Preparatory Division
records.summary: The non-credit music and dance division of Temple's Boyer College of Music and Dance. It teaches people of every age, from babies to adults, through private lessons, group classes, adult classes and community ensembles, and it runs the Philadelphia String Project for beginning string players.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for private lessons, including Suzuki instruction, a group class for children from infancy through the teen years, an adult class, or a community band, orchestra or choir. Beginning string students in grades 2 to 7 can join the Philadelphia String Project. Join the email list for news.

schedule.text: Private lessons and classes run through the year. The Philadelphia String Project meets on Saturday mornings. Community ensembles rehearse one evening a week for about two hours and perform each semester.

locations.label: Presser Hall (Philadelphia String Project location, Boyer College address)

cost.text: Individual lessons are $40 for 30 minutes, $60 for 45 minutes and $80 for 60 minutes (traditional method, per Temple's course listing). The application for individual lessons is free. Some adult classes offer a free intro class. Group class, ensemble and String Project fees are not listed on the pages read.

requirements.gear: Students bring their own instrument for the String Project and the ensembles; the adult guitar class also needs an acoustic guitar and tuner.

first_step.how: Complete the free Individual Music Lessons application in Temple's non-credit course search, and the office will match you with a teacher.
first_step.basis: The String Project needs no audition or prior experience and invites families to open houses, and some adult classes offer a free intro class. Individual lessons need an application first, and the site does not describe a first-day welcome, so this is a 4 rather than a 5.
first_step.what_to_expect: Private lessons are one on one with a teacher, in 30, 45 or 60 minute blocks, and the course listing suggests 30 minutes for children 12 and under. Some adult classes are small and informal, and community ensembles rehearse one evening a week and perform each semester. New students can start partway through a semester, with the fee prorated.
first_visit_tips: Have your instrument, your experience and your availability ready, since the application asks for them.
Choose a 30, 45 or 60 minute lesson; the course listing suggests 30 minutes for children 12 and under.
Ask the office where lessons and classes meet, since the site does not list rooms; the String Project meets at Presser Hall.
Ask about refunds and absences, which are set out in a separate policy document.

records.notes: Lesson rooms and class times are not on the site, so ask the office. The String Project page gives two ZIP codes (19102 and 19122); the record uses 19122, which matches 2001 North 13th Street. The String Project 2026 to 2027 season is open for registration. Its Sept 19, 2026 open house has passed; the next listed open house is Jan 9, 2027, 9 am to 11 am. The programs page also lists the Community Music Scholars Program (Philadelphia students in grades 2 to 12), the Center for Gifted Young Musicians and summer programs; the pages read do not give enough detail to describe them, so they are not in the record. The infant to teen classes page returned 404, so baby and toddler class details are not verified. Adult ensembles require students to read music and have an instrument, except the Rockin' Owls modern music ensemble, which does not require notation. Fetches used: 5 (one 404). Searches used: 0.

records.name: Termite TV Collective
records.summary: A Philadelphia video and media art collective that makes experimental video, shows its work in galleries and screenings, and airs its show on PhillyCAM. Its Places of Power project uses virtual and augmented reality to tell neighborhood stories.
records.what_you_do: Watch the collective's show on PhillyCAM on Friday nights, go to a gallery show or screening, or sign up for its newsletter to hear about the next event.

schedule.text: Termite TV airs on PhillyCAM on Fridays at 11:30 pm. Gallery shows and screenings are announced one at a time on the collective's website.

locations.label: Collective address (from IRS records, not confirmed as open to visitors)

cost.text: Gallery access was free at a past exhibition. The site does not list a cost for other events.

first_step.how: Sign up for the newsletter on the Termite website to hear about the next show or screening.
first_step.basis: Past exhibitions and screenings were open to the public at no charge, and the newsletter is the one public way in shown on the site. The site does not describe how to join the collective or how its workshops work.
first_step.what_to_expect: Termite TV's show airs on PhillyCAM on Friday nights, so you can watch it without going out. Gallery shows and screenings have been open to the public, and the site does not describe a typical event or any sign-up beyond the newsletter.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for the newsletter on the Termite website to get event dates.
Check the date and place before you go, since the site lists events one at a time.
The site lists no email or phone number, so the newsletter is the only stated way in.
If you cannot get to an event, watch the PhillyCAM show on Friday at 11:30 pm.

records.notes: termite.org is thin. The home page returned no readable text, and /mound holds the only readable content: video works, a newsletter sign-up, and two listings dated Oct 10, 2026 (El Bembé, and an event titled as postponed to Oct 10). The listings give no place, price or sign-up, so they are used only as evidence of activity. No about, event or contact pages were found. The PhillyCAM member profile is undated (labeled April), so the Friday 11:30 pm airing time may have changed. The 412 Belgrade St address comes from IRS filings, not a public listing; the public shows found were at Cherry Street Pier, which is not added as a location because it is a venue. The contact name from IRS filings was removed because the group does not publish it. One general search found a 2023 PORTALS exhibition at Cherry Street Pier and no other 2026 event. Fetches used: 6. Leads not made into records are listed in leads_only.

records.name: The Arc of Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that advocates for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities and their families. It runs parent training sessions on special education topics, Zoom drop-in hours for school planning help, and a youth leadership program.
records.what_you_do: Join a Zoom Ask the Advocate drop-in hour for school planning help, go to a parent IEP training on topics such as parent rights and evaluations, or ask about the youth leadership program for people ages 14 to 21 with disabilities. Families can also send the online intake form to ask for help and connections to other services.

schedule.text: Parent IEP training sessions and Zoom Ask the Advocate drop-in hours are held on dates the site posts and changes. Check the site before you plan to attend.

cost.text: Individual membership is listed at $20 a year. Training fees are not listed on the pages read, and the membership form uses monthly recurring payment wording, so ask how billing works before you pay.

access.notes: The site has no ASL or wheelchair statement. Ask the office about accommodations.

first_step.how: Register for a Zoom Ask the Advocate drop-in hour through the registration link on arcphiladelphia.org.
first_step.basis: Drop-in Zoom hours, a listed phone line and an online intake form are open to families and individuals, but the site does not describe a welcome for newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: An Ask the Advocate hour is a drop-in Zoom call: you register, join, ask about school planning or IEPs, and leave when you are done. The parent IEP trainings cover topics such as parent rights, evaluations, writing goals and assistive technology, and the site posts slides for some sessions as downloads. The site does not say how long a session lasts or what it costs.
first_visit_tips: Use the registration link on the Arc's home page for the Zoom hour, and write down your questions about your child's school plan before you join.
The main office is at 2350 West Westmoreland Street, 19140, but the site does not list office hours or transit, so call 215-229-4550 first.
When you call, ask about sign language, wheelchair access and other accommodations, since the site does not describe them.
Ask about training fees and how membership is billed before you register, since the site does not list training costs.

records.notes: SpArc Philadelphia's site (sparcphilly.org) describes itself as a family of organizations serving people with intellectual and developmental disabilities since 1948. It lists The Arc of Philadelphia as its rights and advocacy organization, at the same address and phone number. Confirm the name and the relationship before publishing; this record keeps The Arc's name. SpArc Services is a separate entity and is in leads_only. The Oct 13, 2026 information session was cancelled (announced Oct 5, 2026), and a May 19, 2026 session was also cancelled (announced May 12, 2026); no session dates are in the record. The volunteer page routes only to special-event, day-of-service and college practicum contacts, and says volunteer groups are not being taken, with no date given, so volunteering is left out of what_you_do. The IEP training series page gives no dates and mentions a grant that suggests past sessions. The membership form lists a $20 individual option, plus $250 lifetime and $150 business options. The IRS contact name was removed because the group does not publish it. The Ask the Advocate page guessed at /resourcessection/ask-the-advocate.html returned 404, so the hour details come from the home page link. Fetches used: 5 (one 404).

notes: Seven records written, all with verdict publish. Searches used: 1 of 1 (a general search on Termite TV). Fetches used: 36, including 3 guessed paths that returned 404. The TeamSnap and Zoom registration pages were not opened and no form was submitted. Points for the owner: (1) Temple Contemporary is a university gallery with no public volunteer or class program, published as a free place to visit, so decide whether venues belong in the directory. (2) The Arc of Philadelphia is part of the SpArc Philadelphia family at the same address and phone, so confirm the name. (3) Team Up Philly's office is in Narberth, outside Philadelphia, while its programs meet in Philadelphia. (4) Contact names for Termite TV and The Arc came from IRS data and were removed, because the groups do not publish them. (5) Leads not turned into records, with reasons: PhillyCAM (a media center, not in this batch, only its Termite profile read), SpArc Services (separate entity, no website address found on the pages read), Cherry Street Pier (venue).
